claims.text: The route deviation is established on the trace, not on the rider's impression. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field where it disagrees with the rounded trip-record copy, and the trace records 8.77 km against a booked optimal of 5.6 km — an excess of 3.17 km, or 56.6% of the optimal route. Both establishment tests pass: 56.6% is greater than the 20% test and 3.17 km is greater than the 0.8 km test. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own measurements, and I cite the trace figure rather than the 8.8 km convenience copy on the trip record.

The excess is not merely established, it is MATERIAL: 56.6% is greater than the 50% materiality threshold set by POL-RD-01, so the deviation is additionally a material deviation and the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06 is mandatory on this file. The driver's own device telemetry, at 100% coverage with no gaps, carries the measurement; there is nothing impaired about it.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has discharged it. Limb (a): trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00502, and the vehicle start on the trip record (2026-08-21T20:46:40+08:00) matches the first fix on the trace to the second, so the artifacts demonstrably describe the same trip. Limb (b): the excess of 3.17 km at 56.6% clears the POL-RD-01 threshold and is measured from an unimpaired trace.

The rider's own profile does not weaken this claim, and I cite only the field POL-RD-08 names: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. The special corroboration requirement POL-RD-08 imposes where a rider has four or more claims and one or fewer substantiated is nowhere near engaged on this profile, so the ordinary standard applies. No other rider profile field is relied on, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

On POL-RD-02 arithmetic, the baseline refund is 6.60, and the ruling must state it line by line as the clause requires. charged_total is 17.92. recomputed_fare is (3.80 base + 0.75 x 5.6 km optimal + 0.28 x 9.0 min optimal) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which the trip record does not even carry as a field, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP on the optimal route, plus zero fixed surcharges, plus zero waiting time, less zero promo: 10.52 + 0.80 = 11.32. Refund = 17.92 - 11.32 = 6.60, which is far above the 0.50 de minimis floor, so a refund is owed and NO_ACTION is not available.

The POL-RD-06 pattern is ESTABLISHED on the field the clause names and on no other: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 4, which is 3 or more. The near-synonym lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (6) is deliberately not cited, because POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 fix the trailing-90-day field as the one that counts. This driver has been flagged four times in ninety days, and this trip is the fifth recorded excess.

Because the pattern is established and this deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total rather than the 6.60 POL-RD-02 partial. The two figures should be printed side by side so the uplift is auditable: POL-RD-02 gives 6.60; the uplifted figure is 17.92, the whole charged_total. The only carve-out POL-RD-06(b) makes is for government-set and third-party pass-through lines settled under POL-RD-09, and there are none here — ERP is 0.00 and the trip originates at Sentosa Gateway, not an airport, so no airport surcharge line exists. The rider should pay nothing for this ride.

POL-RD-06(c) additionally sends this driver to driver-conduct review, and that referral is recorded in the ruling's referrals list. Under POL-GEN-03 a referral is not an escalation: it never suppresses or delays the money, so the FULL_REFUND issues alongside it. Four 90-day deviation flags on a driver with 110 completed trips in 30 days is exactly the serial pattern the clause exists to surface.

No chat-based exoneration is open to the driver. The chat log for this trip is empty — message_count 0, no messages at all, and therefore no waypoint_hint on which the POL-RD-04 corroboration test could ever be run. Nothing in the record shows the rider asked for a hill route, so the excess is not reduced by one metre under POL-RD-04, and the driver's assertion that he 'follows the app most of the time' is unsupported by any message from this rider.

POL-RD-05 cannot reduce the excess either. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null: there was no pin move, no re-quote and no platform-directed bay assignment, so the booked 5.6 km optimal stands as the baseline and no distance is excluded from the excess before POL-RD-01 is applied.

This was not a pooled trip, so no part of the extra distance is excused as co-rider collection. The trip record shows vehicle_type RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, and carries no matched-itinerary baseline; the solo optimal of 5.6 km is therefore the correct and only baseline, and POL-RD-12 provides no reduction.

The driver's road-works excuse is weightless on this record. The only traffic artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00502-01, is MISSING: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload, and its own issue detail records that no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 can only exonerate where an advisory actually names a road the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window; no such comparison can be run here, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver's account of 'a road works sign near Telok Blangah' is an uncited traffic excuse, and it neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

This case does not escalate. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: EV-GPS-00502 has 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, a 10-second sampling interval equal to the 10-second expected interval and 145 fixes, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. Nor does POL-RD-10(5) fire on the missing advisory, because the driver cites no advisory identifier at all: under POL-RD-13 an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. The deviation stands at the measured figure and the refund issues; the missing advisory merely makes the excuse weightless.

There is no pass-through line that could inflate or reduce this award, and the ruling should say so expressly. The fare breakdown itemises ERP and tolls at 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries set, so no off-route gantry charge exists to be refunded as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09 and, equally, no ERP line is comprehended in the refund that would have to be added back on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The rider's remedy is the distance and time refund, uplifted under POL-RD-06(b), with nothing carved out.

One point I do not press: the claim text asks for refunds on three earlier rides as well. No artifact in this bundle describes any other trip, and the contested amount on this file is the 17.92 charged for TRP-00502 and nothing more. I rest the rider's case on this trip's evidence, which is sufficient on its own.

claims.text: Only TRP-00502 is in evidence. The rider's demand for a refund 'for the other ones too' and her invitation to examine the driver's history identify no trip and cite no evidence ID for any ride but this one. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded, and under POL-GEN-01 no profile field may carry an adverse finding about this trip. The contested sum is therefore the SGD 17.92 charged on TRP-00502 and nothing beyond it.

POL-RD-01 fixes the measuring stick. The governing length is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, and the trip_record's 8.8 km is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. On the governing figure of 8.77 km against a booked optimal of 5.60 km, the excess is 3.17 km, not the 3.2 km the trip record would suggest. The rider's case must be measured at its lowest, from the trace.

Whatever issues must be arithmetic on the fare breakdown, not the whole fare. Under POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is SGD 11.32 — base 3.80 + 0.75 x 5.60 km + 0.28 x 9.0 min, times the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, toll or surcharge lines — so the loss is SGD 17.92 less SGD 11.32 = SGD 6.60. That sum is 36.8% of the amount charged, far below the 90% share at which POL-RD-02 would itself convert a partial refund into a full one. The rider's demand for the entire SGD 17.92 exceeds her measured loss by SGD 11.32.

Nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. POL-RD-09(1) provides that off-route ERP is already comprehended in a POL-RD-02 refund and must never be counted twice. This fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines at all (off-optimal-route ERP total SGD 0.00) and no airport surcharge, because the trip did not originate at an airport. There is accordingly no billing-integrity correction to make under POL-RD-09(4), and no pass-through line by which the distance-and-time figure can be inflated.

The further uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is discretionary — the clause 'licenses' a full refund, it does not compel one — and it should not be exercised on this record. The deviation crosses the 50% percentage band of POL-RD-01, but its excess of 3.17 km is less than half the 8.0 km absolute figure that carries the same MATERIAL label: this is the bottom edge of materiality, not the serial long-haul the uplift is aimed at. If the uplift is nonetheless applied, POL-RD-06(b) requires the SGD 6.60 POL-RD-02 figure and the uplifted figure to be stated side by side so that the SGD 11.32 of deterrent uplift is visible on the face of the ruling.

The driver's explanation cannot be tested on this record, and that gap should not be turned into an aggravating factor against him. The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00502-01 is a MISSING artifact — status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — with no payload, and the driver's statement names no advisory identifier. Under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so the absence neither exonerates the driver nor triggers POL-RD-10(5); but the same missing platform record is what leaves the hill route at Telok Blangah untestable, and the driver should not be penalised beyond the arithmetic for a gap in the platform's own data. The chat log is empty (0 messages), so there is no admission by the driver to aggravate the position either.

Any pattern the rider invites the tribunal to draw must be drawn on the clause-named field and no other. POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 name driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags, which stands at 6, is context only and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure. The pattern test can be met only on the clause-named counter, and POL-RD-06 itself forbids using any pattern to establish that this particular trip deviated — that finding must rest on POL-RD-01 and this trip's own trace.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this ruling concerns trip TRP-00502 only.

THE MEASUREMENT. POL-RD-01 requires the threshold test on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded 8.8 km convenience copy on the trip record. The trace records 8.77 km against a booked optimal route of 5.60 km. The excess is 3.17 km, or 56.6% of the optimal route: both establishment tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), and the 50% mark is crossed, so the deviation is also MATERIAL. The trace carries no defect for policy purposes (100% coverage, 145 fixes, 10-second cadence, no gaps), so no POL-RD-07(a)-(c) impairment arises and the rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00502 and their timestamps agree.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The bundle contains no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00502-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no payload. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's account of 'a road works sign near Telok Blangah' is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory on file, POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the account carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and reduces no kilometre of the excess. The chat log is empty (0 messages), so POL-RD-04 gives no reduction; no amendment marker exists under POL-RD-05; and the vehicle was RYDE_PLUS, not a pooled trip under POL-RD-12.

THE MONEY, LINE BY LINE. POL-RD-02 recomputes the fare on the booked optimal route: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 5.60 km + 0.28 x 9.0 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 11.32. charged_total 17.92 less recomputed_fare 11.32 = 6.60. That is 36.8% of the charge, below the 90% at which POL-RD-02 would itself convert to a full refund, and well above the 0.50 de minimis floor. No ERP, toll or surcharge line exists to be added or carved out (off-optimal-route ERP total 0.00; the trip did not originate at an airport), so nothing is added on top of, or subtracted from, that figure under POL-RD-09.

Under POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is SGD 11.32 — base 3.80 + 0.75 x 5.60 km + 0.28 x 9.0 min, times the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, toll or surcharge lines — so the loss is SGD 17.92 less SGD 11.32 = SGD 6.60. That sum is 36.8% of the amount charged, far below the 90% share at which POL-RD-02 would itself convert a partial refund into a full one. The rider's demand for the entire SGD 17.92 exceeds her measured loss by SGD 11.32.

Nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. POL-RD-09(1) provides that off-route ERP is already comprehended in a POL-RD-02 refund and must never be counted twice. This fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines at all (off-optimal-route ERP total SGD 0.00) and no airport surcharge, because the trip did not originate at an airport. There is accordingly no billing-integrity correction to make under POL-RD-09(4), and no pass-through line by which the distance-and-time figure can be inflated.

The further uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is discretionary — the clause 'licenses' a full refund, it does not compel one — and it should not be exercised on this record. The deviation crosses the 50% percentage band of POL-RD-01, but its excess of 3.17 km is less than half the 8.0 km absolute figure that carries the same MATERIAL label: this is the bottom edge of materiality, not the serial long-haul the uplift is aimed at. If the uplift is nonetheless applied, POL-RD-06(b) requires the SGD 6.60 POL-RD-02 figure and the uplifted figure to be stated side by side so that the SGD 11.32 of deterrent uplift is visible on the face of the ruling.

The driver's explanation cannot be tested on this record, and that gap should not be turned into an aggravating factor against him. The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00502-01 is a MISSING artifact — status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — with no payload, and the driver's statement names no advisory identifier. Under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so the absence neither exonerates the driver nor triggers POL-RD-10(5); but the same missing platform record is what leaves the hill route at Telok Blangah untestable, and the driver should not be penalised beyond the arithmetic for a gap in the platform's own data. The chat log is empty (0 messages), so there is no admission by the driver to aggravate the position either.

Any pattern the rider invites the tribunal to draw must be drawn on the clause-named field and no other. POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 name driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags, which stands at 6, is context only and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure. The pattern test can be met only on the clause-named counter, and POL-RD-06 itself forbids using any pattern to establish that this particular trip deviated — that finding must rest on POL-RD-01 and this trip's own trace.
